title: Degree agrees with the degree of file 06
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, $C$ a proper smooth
curve over $k$, and $D$ a
divisor of $C$ which is effective. Then the
degree $\deg(\mathcal{O}_C(D))$ of
Definition [def-pc-degree-line-bundle]
equals $\deg D$ of [def-sc-pic0] (for $k$ algebraically closed
where it is defined). In particular for a $k$-rational point $P$,
$\deg(\mathcal{O}_C([P]))=1$.

proof.text: Assume the algebraically closed, smooth connected-curve setting in which [def-sc-pic0] is defined. For the divisor-theoretic line bundle $\mathcal O_C(D)$, [lem-sc-riemann-roch](1) gives $\chi(C,\mathcal O_C(D))=\deg_{\mathrm{SC}}\mathcal O_C(D)+1-g$ and $\chi(C,\mathcal O_C)=1-g$. By [def-sc-pic0], $\deg_{\mathrm{SC}}[\mathcal O_C(D)]=\deg D$. The canonical isomorphism [lem-pc-divisor-line-bundle-agrees-sc] identifies this line bundle with the effective-Cartier-divisor construction used in [def-pc-degree-line-bundle]; isomorphic line bundles have isomorphic cohomology. Subtracting the two Euler characteristics in [def-pc-degree-line-bundle] therefore yields $\deg_{\mathrm{PC}}(\mathcal O_C(D))=\deg D$.

source.place: node lem-pc-degree-agrees-sc, order 812; proof sentence identifying the two degree notions

proof.text: For a $k$-rational point $P$, the divisor $[P]$ is effective and [def-sc-pic0] states that the class of $\mathcal O_C([P])$ (the class of a $k$-rational point) has degree $\deg[P]=1$. Step 1 applied to $D=[P]$ (with the canonical identification [lem-pc-divisor-line-bundle-agrees-sc] of the two modules $\mathcal O_C([P])$) gives $\deg(\mathcal O_C([P]))=\deg[P]=1$.
